\begin{chapstatus}{Roadmap of this chapter}
By the end of the chapter you can:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item tell a combinational machine from a sequential one
\item use decoders, multiplexers, comparators and parity
\item explain the ALU as parallel units and a multiplexer
\end{enumerate}
It builds on: only the setup of Chapter~\ref{ch:setup}. Next: Chapter~\ref{ch:verm1p2}.
\par\smallskip\textbf{Looking back, looking ahead.} In Lecture 02 an instruction was a 32-bit number, and the processor somehow knew what to do with it. Today a decoder reads a field of that number, funct3, and drives the multiplexer that picks the ALU's result. Lecture 19 describes all the fields and the fetch, decode, execute cycle. \emph{Recall:} Which part of the word of an instruction tells the ALU to add rather than to compute an AND?
\end{chapstatus}
